symptom: After upgrading compost to the release whose notes say Jev now refuses incomplete answers, `uv run scripts/jev.py` still crashes with `KeyError: 'other'` on a handful of files. The same files crash every run, instantly, while every other file scores normally. On another machine with a fresh install the same files score fine.
red_herring: The Jev API is still dropping answers for those files and the new missing-answer guard in Jev.ask has a bug, so the incomplete response slips through to the caller.
root_cause: Jev.ask in scripts/jevtools/core.py returned any cache hit unconditionally, before the missing-answer check. ~/.cache/compost/jev-cache.json still held partial answer dicts written by the older version, so those files never reached the API or the guard and the caller indexed a missing question.
cause_check: Note that the failing runs make no API request (the cached counter goes up), then inspect the entry for that file in ~/.cache/compost/jev-cache.json and see it lacks the 'other' key.

symptom: After the Jev model behind compost's semantic lint was updated, rerunning `uv run scripts/lint/run_eval.py` prints exactly the same precision and recall per threshold as before the update, down to the second decimal. The run also finishes with `412 judgments in 0.3s`, where the first-ever run took several minutes.
red_herring: The Jev model update hasn't actually rolled out to this API key (still served the old model), so identical scores are genuine.
root_cause: run_eval.judge called jev_lint.run, which always built the default shared Cache at ~/.cache/compost/jev-cache.json. Every eval case was a cache hit from the previous run, so the eval reported the old model's answers and timed cache reads rather than querying the live API.
cause_check: Check whether the eval makes any API calls at all (e.g. move ~/.cache/compost/jev-cache.json aside and rerun, or count client calls) and see the numbers and timing change.

symptom: Running compost:prune's `python scripts/doc_refs.py scan --exclude 'plugins/*'` (and also `--exclude plugins/`) on the marketplace repo still lists dozens of deep docs like `plugins/compost/skills/build/references/fitting-a-test-in.md` as prune candidates. Trying `--exclude '*.md'` hides them, but it also hides `plugins/compost/README.md`, which is supposed to always be a kept core doc.
red_herring: The shell is expanding the glob before doc_refs.py sees it, so the pattern needs different quoting.
root_cause: scan() matched exclude patterns with PurePosixPath.match, which anchors from the right, so no pattern could mean 'everything under plugins/' from the repo root. Exclusion was also checked before core-ness, so a broad exclude could drop a core README.
cause_check: Evaluate PurePosixPath('plugins/compost/skills/build/references/x.md').match('plugins/*') in a REPL and see it is False, since matching is right-anchored, then read how scan applies exclude before core.

symptom: Running compost's diagnose helper `find-polluter.sh stray-output.db 'uv run pytes' tests/test_*.py` steps through every file `[1/40] ... [40/40]` in well under a second and ends with `No test file created stray-output.db.` The agent concluded no test pollutes, but the stray file definitely appears when the full suite runs.
red_herring: The pollution only happens through test interaction (ordering/shared fixtures across files), so running each file in isolation can never reproduce it.
root_cause: find-polluter.sh discarded each run's stdout and stderr and ignored the exit status, so a test command that could not run (typo'd or missing runner, exit 126/127) looked like a clean test file. Every 'run' did nothing and the script reported no polluter.
cause_check: Run the test command by hand on one file (or drop the `> /dev/null 2>&1`) and look at its exit status and stderr.

symptom: Running compound-capture to record a solution, the agent stops at Step 6 with `Error: File does not exist: .../skills/compound-capture/references/solution-template.md` and the same for `references/yaml-schema.md`. `ls` of the skill directory shows a `references` entry, and reinstalling the plugin from the marketplace does not help.
red_herring: The plugin cache is stale or CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT points at an old install, so paths resolve against the wrong directory.
root_cause: A Goal/Dependencies restructure (5ef1040) deleted the template and schema files but left skills/compound-capture/references as a symlink to ../compound-knowledge/references, which no longer exists. The skill names files the plugin doesn't ship.
cause_check: Run `ls -la skills/compound-capture/` and `readlink -e references` and see the references entry is a dangling symlink.

symptom: After installing compost from the marketplace, `/compost:implement` says it will hand each issue to compost:build, then reports `Unknown skill: compost:build`. The plugin lists 12 skills instead of 13. In the author's local checkout everything works and the full test suite passes.
red_herring: The build skill's SKILL.md frontmatter is malformed (bad name or description), so the plugin loader silently skips it.
root_cause: The repo's root .gitignore has a generic Python `build/` rule that also matched plugins/compost/skills/build/, so the skill was never committed or published. Local runs passed because the untracked copy existed on disk.
cause_check: Run `git check-ignore -v plugins/compost/skills/build/SKILL.md` (or `git ls-files plugins/compost/skills/build`) and see it is ignored by `.gitignore:build/`.

symptom: With autonomous-sdlc installed, calling EnterWorktree from a directory that is not a git repo fails with `ENOENT: no such file or directory, chdir '{"systemMessage": "[WorktreeCreate] New worktree: path= branch="}'`. Inside git repos EnterWorktree works. Also, every line in `.sdlc/events/hook-events.jsonl` has `"worktree_path":"","branch":""`.
red_herring: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT contains a space and the hook command is word-split, so the hook script fails and the harness ends up with garbage.
root_cause: hooks/scripts/worktree-create.sh echoed a {"systemMessage": ...} JSON blob on stdout, but for WorktreeCreate the harness treats stdout as the absolute path of a hook-created worktree; outside git it delegates creation to the hook and chdirs to that line. The script also parsed worktree_path/branch, which the event doesn't carry (it sends worktree_name/base_ref), so the logged fields were empty.
cause_check: Read the WorktreeCreate hook contract (stdout = created worktree path) and run the script by hand with a sample event to see it prints the JSON blob to stdout.

symptom: In Claude Desktop background sessions, none of autonomous-sdlc's hooks seem to run: the loop's Stop hook never re-prompts, auto-approve never fires, and the transcript shows hook errors like `bash: /Users/josh/Library/Application: No such file or directory`. The exact same plugin version works fine in a terminal Claude Code session on the same machine.
red_herring: Background sessions don't load plugin hooks (or lack the bash PATH), so it's a harness limitation of local-agent mode.
root_cause: hooks/hooks.json invoked each script as `bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/scripts/foo.sh` without quotes. In background sessions the plugin root lives under `~/Library/Application Support/...`, so the shell split the path at the space and bash looked for a nonexistent file.
cause_check: Print CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT in a background session and compare it with the terminal session's, noting the space, then look at how hooks.json quotes it.

symptom: After updating autonomous-sdlc to 2.1.x, `/sdlc` on a feature started last week prints `RESUME state=BUILD iteration=7` and carries on, but when the loop reaches REVIEW the gate's `python3 -c` one-liner dies with `KeyError: 'review'`. Features started after the update reach REVIEW and pass the gate normally.
red_herring: The state.json got corrupted or partially written during the plugin update (e.g. an interrupted save), so the fix is to repair or delete it.
root_cause: The REVIEW gate reads state['review'], a key added in 2.1.0. cmd_init's resume branch in scripts/sdlc_state.py returned immediately without backfilling it, so a state.json created under 2.0.0 never got a review block.
cause_check: Open the old feature's .sdlc/state.json, see it is valid JSON with no 'review' key, and compare it with a state.json from a freshly initialized loop.

symptom: Running review-diff on a feature branch with 6 commits, `python scripts/serve.py --base orign/main` prints `NO_CHANGES` and exits, so the agent tells the user the branch has nothing to review. `git log origin/main..HEAD` clearly lists the 6 commits. Separately, in a brand-new repo with no commits yet, staged files never appear in the viewer.
red_herring: The three-dot `base...HEAD` comparison is wrong: the merge-base resolves to HEAD (e.g. the branch was already merged or rebased), so the diff is legitimately empty.
root_cause: _run_git in scripts/collect.py ignored git's return code, so a failed `git diff` (unknown ref `orign/main`, or `git diff HEAD` in a repo with no commits) produced empty stdout that collect_diff parsed as no changes.
cause_check: Run the underlying `git diff --no-prefix orign/main...HEAD` by hand and see it exits 128 with `fatal: ambiguous argument`.

symptom: Running `/compost:review-changes` with `{issue: 66}`, the Spec axis reports blockers like `AC-3 not implemented: export endpoint missing`, but issue #66 has no AC about exports. The returned specSource says `#58`, an issue that was discussed earlier in the same conversation. Re-running in a fresh session grades against #66 correctly.
red_herring: `gh issue view 66` is returning the wrong issue (bad repo context or GH_REPO pointing elsewhere).
root_cause: In workflows/review-changes.js the Spec axis's source and the returned specSource came from whatever issue the scoping agent chose to fetch, not from args.issue. The agent followed the conversation's mention of #58, and nothing compared the fetched issue's number with the one passed.
cause_check: Look at the scope stage's returned spec (source/text) and see it is #58's text even though input.issue was 66, then check where specSource is assigned.

symptom: compost:review reported `Standards: reviewed: 4 findings raised, 0 survived, 3 refuted; worst none` and handed off to compost:finish. The refuted blocker's `refutedBecause` list is empty, and the run log shows the skeptic agents erroring on a rate limit. When the user ran the review again the same blocker survived.
red_herring: The skeptic prompt is too aggressive ('when you are uncertain, it is refuted'), so skeptics are refuting real findings.
root_cause: In workflows/review-changes.js, survives() set survived = cast.length > 0 && ..., so a finding whose skeptic votes all failed (none cast) fell into refuted. A failed reviewer or unfetchable issue likewise looked like a clean axis, and the run carried no completeness flag for the review skill to check.
cause_check: Look at the refuted finding's votes and note zero votes were cast (empty reasons), then read how the verdict is computed when cast is empty.

symptom: `uv run scripts/pile.py status` for the superpowers source lists bogus paths under compost skills such as `skills/writing`, `plans/SKILL.md`, and says `37 changed files feed no compost skill`, though upstream only changed about 12 files. A skill that upstream renamed shows up as an unmapped add, not under the compost skill it fed.
red_herring: The `feeds` prefixes in pile.toml are stale or wrongly written, so files are mismatched to skills.
root_cause: git_compare in scripts/pile.py ran `git diff --name-only pin head` and split the output on whitespace, so paths with spaces broke into fragments. With rename detection on, a renamed file was listed under its new path only, so it no longer matched the feed prefix.
cause_check: Run the same `git -C <clone> diff --name-only <pin> <head>` by hand and compare its lines with what pile.py reports, noting paths containing spaces.

symptom: During an autonomous-sdlc fix task, the agent's Edit to `specs/checkout-plan.md` is denied with the test-lock message saying test files are locked during fix tasks, so it can't update the plan. Meanwhile in the same loop, `git push origin HEAD:main` went through without the destructive-command guard firing, though `git push origin main` is blocked.
red_herring: The hook matchers in hooks.json are wrong: the PreToolUse guard isn't matching Bash for some invocations and the test-lock matches every Edit.
root_cause: hooks/scripts/test-lock.sh listed `specs` in TEST_DIRS, so anything under specs/ (the loop's own intent/spec/plan docs) counted as a test file. The deny-destructive.sh main-push regex only caught `[remote] main` and missed refspec forms like HEAD:main, feature:main, refs/heads/main, and +main.
cause_check: Feed sample events through the two scripts: test-lock with file_path specs/checkout-plan.md, and deny-destructive with `git push origin HEAD:main`, and read TEST_DIRS and the push regex.

symptom: After an autonomous-sdlc feature reached DONE and the PR opened, typing a bare `/loop` (expecting Claude Code's built-in PR-maintenance loop) restarted the old feature's iteration ritual. After upgrading the plugin, `/loop` in that project fails with `python3: can't open file '/Users/josh/.claude/plugins/cache/.../2.3.0/scripts/sdlc_state.py'`, and starting a new increment still shows the previous feature's name in the loop prompt.
red_herring: Claude Code is caching the old /loop prompt in its own session state, so restarting Claude Code should pick up the new one.
root_cause: scripts/sdlc_state.py wrote .claude/loop.md once at init and never overwrote it, with the feature name and the absolute path to sdlc_state.py baked in, and never removed it on DONE/BLOCKED. A bare /loop keeps running that project file, with its stale feature and plugin path.
cause_check: Open .claude/loop.md in the project and see the old feature name and old versioned plugin path baked in, then check whether init or transition ever rewrites or deletes it.

symptom: compost:setup reported it wrote docs/agents/issue-tracker.md, domain.md and testing.md and made a `chore: configure agent skills` commit. On a teammate's fresh clone, compost:slice says `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md missing; run compost:setup`. `git show --stat HEAD` for the setup commit lists only AGENTS.md.
red_herring: Setup's commit step stages only AGENTS.md (an explicit `git add AGENTS.md`), so the docs/agents files were never added.
root_cause: The repo's .gitignore had a broad `agents/` rule that also matches docs/agents/, so `git add` silently skipped the files and the commit left them out. compost:setup's commit step never checked its written files against gitignore.
cause_check: Run `git check-ignore -v docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` in the original repo and see it reported as ignored by `.gitignore:N:agents/`.
